name: Norway
summary: A casket coming into Norway must travel in approved packaging (a metal inner coffin for transport from outside the Nordic countries) with the death documents required by the country of departure, and the Norwegian embassy or consulate abroad issues the documents needed for repatriation. The receiving funeral home must collect the coffin as soon as possible after arrival.
documents: Death certificate from the country of death (legalised or apostilled where the Norwegian embassy requires it)
Transport documents or laissez-passer issued in the country of departure
Documents issued by the Norwegian embassy or consulate for the repatriation
Cause of death, which may be sent to the municipal physician in a sealed envelope
Coffin marking with name, date of birth, date of death, sender and recipient
coffin: Norwegian regulation FOR-1998-04-03-327 requires transport in a coffin with a packaging method approved by the Directorate of Health for air transport. Its commentary states that a metal inner coffin is required for transport to and from countries outside the Nordic region, in line with the Council of Europe agreement on the transfer of corpses and IATA practice; a body bag may be used between Nordic countries under an agreement between funeral associations and airlines. The coffin must be marked with the deceased's identity and the sender and recipient. No Norwegian witness to sealing is required by the regulation.
embalming: Not required by Norwegian rules for entry. Embalming falls under the hygiene rules of the regulation and must be done by qualified personnel. Not recommended when death was caused by a serious infectious disease.
consular: The Norwegian embassy or consulate in the country of death issues the necessary documents for the repatriation and registers the death in the Norwegian population register; the original foreign death certificate must be handed to the embassy (some embassies require it to be legalised or apostilled). The regulation refers to the Council of Europe agreement on the transfer of corpses (Strasbourg 1973) for transport between member states.
arrival: The recipient (usually a Norwegian funeral home) must collect the coffin as soon as possible. Ideally only the municipal physician at the point of arrival is told the cause of death. If a serious infectious disease makes re-coffining risky, it must be done at a forensic institute or hospital pathology department. Funeral homes in Norway often transfer the body to a coffin meeting Norwegian burial requirements.
pouch: A body bag is allowed for transport between Nordic countries under an agreement between funeral associations and airlines; from outside the Nordic region a metal inner coffin is required.
private_aviation: No Norwegian rule specific to private aircraft carrying human remains was found. The general packaging, marking and documentation rules of FOR-1998-04-03-327 apply. Norway is in Schengen but outside the EU customs union, so a flight from outside Schengen must land at an airport with border and customs control.
private_jet_note: Use an airport with border and customs service if arriving from outside Schengen; packaging must meet the Directorate of Health approved method for air transport.
export: Norwegian rules apply until the body leaves Norway. The sender must use packaging approved by the Directorate of Health unless the destination, transit country, airline or a treaty requires otherwise, and must learn the destination's rules. A metal inner coffin is required outside the Nordic region. Where required, death documents for transport abroad are issued by the local police on the basis of the physician's death certificate. Some destinations require embalming, an embalming certificate and an infection-free certificate. The local registry (tingrett) sends a copy of the death certificate to the funeral home.
export_points: Police issue death documents for transport abroad on the basis of the doctor's death certificate
Metal inner coffin required outside the Nordic region
Body bag allowed to Nordic countries under the airline agreement
Embalming only if the destination requires it

at_a_glance.death_certificate: Foreign certificate, given to Norwegian embassy
at_a_glance.coffin: Metal inner coffin from outside Nordic region
at_a_glance.laissez_passer: From departure country under Strasbourg rules

steps.what: Contact the insurer or a funeral home experienced in international repatriation, and the Norwegian embassy.
Obtain the local death certificate and give the original to the Norwegian embassy (legalised if required).
Local funeral home places the body in a metal-lined coffin and obtains the departure country's transport documents.
The Norwegian embassy issues the repatriation documents; book the flight.
Norwegian funeral home collects the coffin as soon as possible and arranges burial or cremation.

key_points: Norway requires a metal inner coffin for transport from outside the Nordic countries
The embassy registers the death in Norway and issues the repatriation papers
The Norwegian foreign service does not pay repatriation costs
authority: Norwegian Directorate of Health (packaging rules); Norwegian embassies and consulates; police (export documents)

name: Poland
summary: To bring a body into Poland you need a permit from the starosta (or mayor / city president) of the district where the burial will take place, and then a certificate from the Polish consul issued on the basis of that permit and the death certificate. The body must travel in a tightly sealed metal coffin inside a wooden case.
documents: Permit (zezwolenie) from the starosta, mayor or city president of the burial district, issued after consulting the district sanitary inspector
Polish consul's certificate (zaświadczenie) allowing the body into Poland
Death certificate (or copy)
Certificate that death was not caused by an infectious disease
Permission to remove the body issued in the country of death
Funeral company declaration that the coffin contains only the remains
coffin: Metal coffin, tightly sealed, with a layer of absorbent material at least 5 cm thick on the bottom, placed in a wooden case so that it cannot move (Polish consulate in Dublin guidance). Who witnesses the sealing abroad is not stated.
embalming: Not mentioned in the official Polish entry guidance; follow the rules of the country of departure.
consular: The Polish consul issues the certificate for bringing the remains into Poland on the basis of the starosta's permit and a copy of the death certificate, at the latest within 3 days of receiving the application and originals (Dublin consulate). A consular fee applies; check the amount with the consulate. Polish translations were not required by the Dublin consulate. Only the spouse, descendants, ascendants, relatives to the 4th degree and in-laws to the 1st degree may apply.
arrival: Bodies from abroad may only be transported by a specialised funeral company. For deaths from certain infectious diseases (e.g. cholera, plague, rabies, yellow fever) the transfer may only be allowed two years after death.
private_aviation: No rule specific to private aircraft was found. The documents and the sealed metal coffin must accompany the body on any flight; Poland is in Schengen, so a flight from outside Schengen must use an airport with border control.
private_jet_note: Obtain the starosta permit and consular certificate before take-off; the documents travel with the coffin.
export: A permit from the competent district (powiatowy) or border state sanitary inspector is required to take a body abroad. It is issued only after documents from the destination and transit countries confirm there is no obstacle to entry or burial. The body must be in a wooden coffin lined with metal or a metal coffin with 5 cm of absorbent material, placed in a sealed wooden crate or other impermeable container; the inspector may require extra precautions and seals the coffin. The death certificate and the deceased's passport are also needed. Permits are not issued for certain infectious diseases until two years after death.
export_points: Permit from the district (powiatowy) sanitary inspector
Destination-country consent needed before the permit is issued
Metal-lined coffin in a sealed outer case, sealed by the inspector
Death certificate and passport required

at_a_glance.coffin: Sealed metal coffin in wooden case

steps.what: Family appoints funeral companies abroad and in Poland.
Apply to the starosta / mayor of the burial district for the import permit (decision within 3 days, no stamp duty).
Obtain the death certificate, non-infectious disease certificate and local removal permit abroad.
Polish consul issues the certificate on the basis of the permit and death certificate.
Coffin sealed (metal coffin in wooden case) and flown to Poland.
Specialised Polish funeral company collects the coffin for burial.

key_points: Two Polish documents are needed: starosta permit and consular certificate
Some infectious diseases block transfer for two years
Only close relatives may apply
authority: Starosta / mayor of the burial district; Polish consul; State Sanitary Inspection (export)

name: Portugal
summary: For a Portuguese citizen who died abroad, the death must be registered with the Portuguese consulate, which draws up an alvará de trasladação (transfer permit) so the remains can be taken to Portugal. Detailed casket and entry rules for Portugal could not be confirmed from official pages; confirm with the consulate and the receiving funeral home.
documents: Death certificate from the country of death
Registration of the death at the Portuguese consulate (for Portuguese nationals)
Alvará de trasladação issued by the Portuguese consulate
Documents required by the country of departure (e.g. removal permit, coffin sealing certificate)
coffin: Not verified on official Portuguese pages. A hermetically sealed metal-lined coffin in a wooden case is the usual international standard; confirm with the consulate.
embalming: Not verified on official Portuguese pages; follow the rules of the departure country and confirm with the consulate.
consular: The Portuguese consulate registers the death and issues the alvará de trasladação. The Consulate-General in London states no appointment is needed; the funeral homes in the UK and Portugal contact the consulate directly. British certificates do not need legalisation or translation for the London consulate. For ashes in a wooden urn the airline may require an alvará and the urn may need to be sealed at the consulate.
arrival: Not verified on official pages. In Portugal funerals normally take place within 72 hours of death (gov.uk), so plan the burial with the receiving funeral home in advance.
private_aviation: No rule specific to private aircraft found. Portugal is in Schengen; a flight from outside Schengen must use an airport with border and customs control.
private_jet_note: Have the consular alvará de trasladação issued before departure.
export: The death is registered at the local civil registry (Assento de Óbito); an international death certificate (Certidão de Óbito Internacional) can be requested. A local funeral director arranges transport and needs the deceased's passport and a completed form with a copy of the applicant's passport. A post mortem, if required, normally takes place within 3 to 4 working days of death. For cremation, permission from the public prosecutor may be needed. Transport permits, coffin and embalming rules are not described on official pages consulted.
export_points: Register the death and request the international death certificate
Funeral director needs the deceased's passport
Post mortem usually within 3-4 working days
Cremation may need public prosecutor approval

at_a_glance.arrival: Funeral home collects; burial usually quick

steps.what: Contact a local funeral home and a funeral home in Portugal.
Obtain the local death certificate.
Funeral homes contact the Portuguese consulate, which registers the death and issues the alvará de trasladação.
Coffin prepared and sealed according to the departure country's rules; flight booked.
Portuguese funeral home collects the coffin and arranges the funeral.

key_points: The consular alvará de trasladação is the key Portuguese document
Portuguese entry casket rules not confirmed from official sources

consular: Not verified; confirm with the Romanian consulate. The Romanian consulate normally transcribes the death for Romanian citizens.

name: Sweden
summary: Sweden approved the Council of Europe Agreement on the Transfer of Corpses (Strasbourg 1973), so a casket arriving from another party travels with the departure country's laissez-passer. In Sweden, burial or cremation of a body brought in from abroad needs a permit from the Police Authority, based on the foreign death certificate.
documents: Death certificate from the competent authority or doctor in the country of death, stating the date and, if possible, the cause of death
Laissez-passer for the corpse from the departure country (Strasbourg Agreement parties) or that country's transport documents
Application for a burial or cremation permit to the Swedish Police Authority (Polismyndigheten)
coffin: Under the Strasbourg Agreement: an impervious coffin with absorbent material, either an outer wooden coffin with walls at least 20 mm thick and a soldered zinc inner coffin, or a single wooden coffin at least 30 mm thick lined with zinc or another self-destroying material; for air transport a purifying device or adequate pressure resistance. Sealing is certified by the departure country's authorities.
embalming: Not required for transport. In Sweden embalming is required only before burial in a church, burial vault or similar space.
consular: Under the Strasbourg Agreement the destination state may not require documents other than the laissez-passer (apart from general transport documents). For countries outside the Agreement, confirm with the Swedish embassy; translation of the foreign death certificate may be requested.
arrival: The Police Authority grants the burial or cremation permit for a body brought into Sweden, sends it to the Tax Agency (Skatteverket) and forwards the foreign death certificate to the National Board of Health and Welfare. A funeral should if possible take place within a month of death.
pouch: Between Nordic countries (Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway) the full coffin rules apply only if the carrier requests it or a doctor so decides after an infectious death; the coffin must still be sealed and sturdy.
private_aviation: No Swedish rule specific to private aircraft found. Swedish rules for air transport of coffins require a pressure-equalising device or a coffin able to withstand pressure changes. Sweden is in Schengen; a flight from outside Schengen must use an airport with border and customs control.
private_jet_note: Coffin needs a pressure-equalising device or pressure-resistant construction for air transport.
export: A body may only leave Sweden with a passersedel (laissez-passer) issued by the Swedish Tax Agency (Skatteverket), which must accompany the body. It is issued once a burial or cremation certificate can be issued and an undertaker certifies the coffin meets the rules and contains only the body and personal effects (not required for Nordic destinations). The form is in Swedish and English or French. The coffin must be moisture-proof with absorbent lining: wooden outer coffin (2 cm) with zinc inner coffin, or 3 cm wooden coffin lined with zinc; for air transport a pressure-equalising device. Infectious deaths require a shroud soaked in antiseptic. A copy of the passersedel certifying export must be returned to Skatteverket within two weeks. Documents commonly provided: death certificate, non-contagious certificate, embalming certificate, freight certificate and soldering (sealing) certificate.
export_points: Passersedel (laissez-passer) from Skatteverket
Undertaker's coffin certificate (zinc-lined, absorbent)
Pressure-equalising device for air transport
Return certified copy to Skatteverket within two weeks

at_a_glance.death_certificate: Foreign certificate with date of death
at_a_glance.consular: No extra documents for Strasbourg parties
at_a_glance.arrival: Funeral within a month if possible

steps.what: Appoint funeral homes abroad and in Sweden.
Obtain the death certificate in the country of death.
Coffin sealed to Strasbourg standards; departure country issues the laissez-passer.
Flight to Sweden with the laissez-passer and death certificate.
Swedish funeral home applies to the Police Authority for the burial or cremation permit.

key_points: Sweden approved the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement
Police issue the burial or cremation permit for bodies brought in
Skatteverket issues the passersedel for bodies leaving Sweden
authority: Swedish Police Authority (entry burial permit); Swedish Tax Agency, Skatteverket (export laissez-passer)

name: Slovakia
summary: Slovakia is bound by the Agreement on the Transfer of Corpses (Strasbourg 1973, notice 11/2003 Coll.), so a casket from another party travels under that agreement with the departure country's laissez-passer. From a non-party state, a corpse passport (pas pre mŕtvolu) from the Slovak embassy or consulate is needed, and the coffin must meet the agreement's standards.
documents: Laissez-passer from the departure country (Strasbourg Agreement parties)
From non-party states: corpse passport (pas pre mŕtvolu) issued by the Slovak embassy or consulate
Death certificate
Documents required by the country of departure
coffin: The coffin must meet the requirements of the Strasbourg Agreement: impervious, with absorbent material, a soldered zinc inner coffin in a wooden outer coffin (or a zinc-lined wooden coffin at least 30 mm thick). The coffin label must carry the deceased's identity.
embalming: Not required by Slovak law for entry. Embalming, preservation and display of the body are prohibited when the person was infected with a dangerous disease at the time of death.
consular: From a state not bound by the agreement, the Slovak diplomatic mission or consulate issues the corpse passport if all requirements of the departure state are met and the coffin meets the agreement's requirements (Act 131/2010 Coll. section 7(3)).
arrival: Slovak funeral services, crematoria and embalmers may accept the remains on the basis of the corpse passport for international transport. Road transport in Slovakia must use a refrigerated hearse.
private_aviation: No rule specific to private aircraft found. Slovakia is in Schengen; a flight from outside Schengen must use an airport with border and customs control.
private_jet_note: From a non-Strasbourg country, obtain the Slovak consular corpse passport before take-off.
export: Within Strasbourg countries, transport follows the agreement. The corpse passport (laissez-passer) is issued by the self-governing region (samosprávny kraj), by the regional public health authority if the deceased had a dangerous infectious disease, or by the Health Care Surveillance Authority if an autopsy was performed (Act 131/2010 section 7(4)). Documents listed by the UK government: international death certificate (or official translation), passport, medical certificate confirming no infectious disease, embalming certificate and the permission for international transport.
export_points: Corpse passport from the self-governing region (or health authority)
Strasbourg-standard sealed zinc-lined coffin
Embalming and non-infection certificates usually requested
International death certificate

at_a_glance.consular: Slovak corpse passport from non-party states

Flight to Slovakia.
Slovak funeral service collects the coffin in a refrigerated hearse.

key_points: Slovakia applies the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement
Slovak consulates issue a corpse passport for non-party countries
Embalming forbidden if death involved a dangerous infectious disease
authority: Slovak self-governing regions; regional public health authorities; Slovak embassies and consulates
